props.name: accept
props.description: The file types to take, in the `accept` attribute's syntax, such as `"image/*,.pdf"`. The picker receives it as it is, and a picked file that fails it reaches `onReject` with `"type"`.

props.name: capture
props.description: The phone camera the browser asks to capture new media with: `"user"` for the front one, `"environment"` for the back.

props.name: children
props.description: The button's label, which names it. The trigger renders the button and a hidden file input with no element around them, so it joins a `ButtonGroup` as a `Button` does.

props.name: directory
props.description: Whether the picker selects a folder. `onSelect` then receives its files.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the button is disabled. A disabled trigger ignores picks.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Whether the picker takes more than one file. Without it, a pick in which more than one file passes `accept` rejects each of those with `"count"`. The trigger checks `accept` first, so it rejects a file that fails `accept` with `"type"`, and that file never counts.

props.name: onReject
props.description: Called when a pick has files that did not pass, with each file and its `reason`. For one pick, it runs right after `onSelect`, in the same task.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called when a pick has files that pass `accept` and the count rule, with those files in a fresh array. A pick in which no file passes does not call it.

props.name: variant
props.description: The fill and text color. The theme sets the `outline` border. `link` looks like an inline text link.

props.name: withIcon
props.description: Whether the button shows the leading icon: a camera with `capture`, a folder with `directory` and a paperclip otherwise. The icon is decorative, so the children name the button.
